findings.evidence: After user selected 'No thanks' to first offer, chatbot immediately presented second offer: 'I really don't want to lose you — how about 3 months of Premium completely free?'
findings.explanation: The system is persistently offering retention deals after the user has already declined the first offer, making it difficult to complete the cancellation process.

findings.evidence: The page displays 'Your account is paused' with a message about a 3-month hold, but the user's goal was to cancel. The only way to correct this is through the small, underlined link 'I asked to cancel, not pause' which is visually weak and easy to miss.
findings.explanation: The system has paused the account instead of canceling it, which is the opposite of what the user requested. The cancellation option is hidden behind a small, underlined link that is not styled as a button, making it difficult to find and use. This is a classic example of sneaking where the outcome is quietly different from what the user chose.

findings.evidence: The 'No thanks' button is visually weaker than the 'Tell me more' button, which is the primary option for the discount offer. The 'No thanks' button is smaller and less prominent, making it harder for the user to decline the offer.
findings.explanation: The 'No thanks' button is visually weaker than the 'Tell me more' button, which is the primary option for the discount offer. This makes it harder for the user to decline the offer and continue with their cancellation, as the 'No thanks' option is less prominent and easier to overlook.

findings.evidence: The 'Confirm it's you' modal requires re-entering email and password with the text 'For your security, please re-enter your account details to continue to Customer Happiness.' This adds an unnecessary step to the cancellation process, forcing the user to re-authenticate before they can proceed with their goal of canceling the subscription.
findings.explanation: Requiring password re-entry is an extra step that adds friction to the cancellation process. While it may be a security measure, it creates an unnecessary barrier for users trying to cancel their subscription, which is a common dark pattern used to make cancellation more difficult.

legal.title: Résiliation en trois clics
legal.summary: Since 1 June 2023 (loi n° 2022-1158), a contract that can be concluded online must be cancellable online through a free, easily accessible feature.

legal.title: Simple mechanism to stop recurring charges
legal.summary: The Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act requires online negative-option sellers to provide simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges. (The FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel rule was vacated in July 2025; ROSCA still applies.)

legal.title: California Automatic Renewal Law
legal.summary: Consumers who sign up online must be able to cancel online, without obstruction.

legal.title: Ban on deceptive interface design by online platforms
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 forbids online platforms from designing interfaces that deceive or manipulate users, including giving more prominence to certain choices, repeatedly requesting a choice already made, and making termination harder than subscribing.

legal.title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
legal.summary: Prohibits misleading and aggressive commercial practices, including non-contractual barriers to terminating a contract.
